newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico to open bidding for Tampico natgas supply.
newsitem.headline: Mexico to open bidding for Tampico natgas supply.

text.p: Mexico's Energy Ministry invited firms to bid for natural gas distribution rights in the region surrounding the city of Tampico in northern Tamaulipas state, beginning April 28, the ministry said on Monday.
The 12-year concession includes the cities of Tampico, Ciudad Madero and Altamira, located on the Panuco river on the Gulf of Mexico, the ministry said in a statement.
Mexico is auctioning off natural gas distribution rights in select regions as part of an effort to boost use of the fuel and develop supply infrastructure.
Bids for the Tampico region will be accepted through June 28, with a winner due to be announced on July 29.

Natural gas in the region is currently provided through 12- to 16-inch ducts connected to a main pipeline that runs through the region. State oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) will continue to control natural gas supply.
The region's population was 515,606 as of the last census count in 1990, with residents expected to surge 1.24 million by 2000, the ministry said.
A consortium of Mexican and U.S. companies - U.S. Enova International, Pacific Enterprises International and Mexico's Proxima Gas - won the first two natural gas supply concessions auctioned.
The winning bidder for another region, in Hermosillo, Sonora state, is expected later this week.
